artists.biography: Belly was an alternative rock band formed in 1991 by former Throwing Muses members Tanya Donelly (who was also in The Breeders) and Fred Abong. The band was based in Boston, Massachusetts, though all of the original members grew up in Newport, Rhode Island. The band consisted of Donelly on lead vocals and guitar, Abong on bass, Tom Gorman on guitar, and Chris Gorman on drums. Tom and Chris, who were brothers, were childhood friends of Donelly's; they had previously played in the hardcore punk band Verbal Assault. On at least one tour date (in February, 1993) in Albany, NY, former Throwing Muses member, Leslie Langston, lent a hand on bass.

perplexity.description:
Belly’s third studio album, Dove, was released on May 4, 2018, marking their first full-length album in 23 years since 1995’s King. Self-released by the band, Dove continues Belly’s legacy in the alternative rock genre, characterized by bright, crunchy guitars, melodic hooks, and wry, introspective lyrics. The album was crafted through a collaborative, long-distance songwriting process, reflecting the band members’ scattered locations, and retains the signature indie-pop sound that defined their earlier work, without chasing contemporary trends.

Musically, Dove is an old-fashioned indie-pop record that stands out for its sincerity and craftsmanship, drawing comparisons to the band’s 1990s output. Critics noted its timeless quality, with many praising its heartfelt songwriting and the band’s ability to reconnect with their original sound after more than two decades. While not a major commercial hit, Dove was well-received by reviewers, who highlighted its emotional resonance and regarded it as a notable achievement for a group reuniting after such a long hiatus. The album reaffirms Belly’s place in the alternative rock canon and serves as a meaningful addition to their discography.
